title: Creamy Tuscan Chicken
subtitle: Sun-dried tomato, spinach, rich cream
description: Sun-dried tomato, spinach, rich cream. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Creamy Tuscan Chicken in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Sear chicken breasts
steps.instruction: Season chicken breasts; sear in olive oil over medium-high 6 minutes per side until 165°F. Rest and slice. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Build Tuscan cream sauce
steps.instruction: In the same pan, sauté garlic and sun-dried tomatoes 1 minute. Add cream and parmesan; simmer until coats a spoon. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Wilt spinach
steps.instruction: Fold spinach into sauce until just wilted — bright green, not army drab. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Creamy Tuscan Chicken onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Serve over pasta or rice
steps.instruction: Return sliced chicken to sauce. Serve over penne or rice with extra parmesan. Creamy Tuscan Chicken should smell like garlic and wine, not boiled cream.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Plate Creamy Tuscan Chicken with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Creamy Tuscan Chicken on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Sun-dried tomato, spinach, rich cream. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — Creamy Tuscan Chicken runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
